sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page orig1234 (Original Costa Rican Sign Language)
sources.note: No descriptive references; cites Woodward 1991 (lexical comparison), Campbell et al. 2022 (endangerment) and Avendaño 2013; notes the language 'has been declining for several decades, without being documented or described'.

sources.citation: Sánchez Avendaño, Carlos. 2013. "Lenguas en peligro en Costa Rica: vitalidad, documentación y descripción." Káñina, Rev. Artes y Letras, Univ. Costa Rica 37(1): 219-250. DOI 10.15517/rk.v37i1.10589
sources.note: Nothing on stress or phonology of OLESCO; states three times (pp. 220, 227, 233) that the original variety of LESCO has never been described or documented (only Woodward 1991, 1992 and Retana 1993 exist, all lexical/historical).

sources.citation: Woodward, James. 1992. "Historical bases of New Costa Rican Sign Language." Revista de Filología y Lingüística de la Universidad de Costa Rica 18(1): 127-132. DOI 10.15517/rfl.v18i1.20071
sources.note: Lexicostatistical comparison only (Swadesh-derived sign list; one OLESCO signer, a deaf 44-year-old woman; 41.8% cognates OLESCO/NLESCO, 25.5% OLESCO/ASL). No phonology, prosody or stress; p. 132 calls for documentation 'as soon as possible' since OLESCO varieties will likely be extinct within a generation.
Stub; cites only Woodward 1991; no structural information.

sources.citation: Retana, P. 1993 (title not given in full; cited by Sánchez Avendaño 2013 on the 1976 relexification of LESCO and community awareness that LESCO differs from ASL).
